sections.text:
There was a poor and simple farmer who lived with his wife on a small farm, and they owned some chickens and geese to live off of their eggs.

One bright day, the farmer went to the bird barn to collect eggs as he did every morning.

When he arrived at a goose's nest, he found something shining with a strange brilliance under the sun's rays!
The farmer approached with curiosity and extended his hand to take the egg. He was surprised that it was very heavy and not like regular eggs. When he examined it carefully, he shouted at the top of his voice in astonishment!
It was an egg made of pure gold and bright yellow!
The farmer ran quickly to his wife carrying the golden egg and shouting: “My wife! Come and see! Our wondrous goose has laid an egg of pure gold! We have become rich!”

The wife did not believe it at first, so they took the egg to a goldsmith in the market to test it. The jeweler assured them that it was the purest type of gold and paid them a high price for it.

The farmer and his wife returned very happy and bought fine food and new clothes.

The next morning, the farmer eagerly went to the goose's nest to check, and how great was his surprise when he found another golden egg waiting for him!
This continued every day; The goose lay only one golden egg for them every morning without interruption.

The farmer sold golden eggs day after day, and began building a large house, buying large lands, and hiring servants, until he became one of the richest people in the village.

But getting rich quickly changed the heart of the farmer and his wife, and greed and avarice began to creep into their minds instead of contentment and gratitude.

One night, the farmer said to his wife while rubbing his hands in greed: “This goose lays one egg every day. This is very slow! If we wait for one egg every day, it will take us a long time to become the richest people in the entire world!”

The greedy wife replied: “You are right! There must be a very huge block of pure gold in the stomach of this strange goose, or perhaps a small gold factory!”

The farmer thought and said with eyes shining with greed: “If we slaughter her and slit her stomach, we will be able to take all the gold at once and become kings in one second, instead of this long wait!”

Wealth and greed blinded them to proper thinking, and they agreed to this evil plan.

Early in the morning, the farmer went carrying a sharp knife, grabbed the poor goose that had made him rich and slaughtered it mercilessly!
When he eagerly cut into her stomach to search for the huge block of gold and the alleged factory, he was deeply shocked and froze in place from the horror of surprise.

He found the inside of its belly, just like the belly of any normal goose! There is not a single gram of gold in it, not even an egg in the making!
The farmer and his wife realized, in a moment of deadly and painful remorse, that because of their greed and foolish greed, they had lost their great source of wealth forever.

The farmer sat crying bitterly next to the goose's corpse, remembering the daily blessing of the egg for which he did not thank God, to learn a harsh historical lesson: Greed and avarice destroy everything, and whoever is not satisfied with the constant little, loses a lot and all at once in a moment of stupidity and heartbreak.
